name: _sparse_csr_sum
description: Representative ATen overload, copied verbatim from the registered schema and NOT an exclusive ABI: aten::_sparse_csr_sum.dim_dtype(Tensor self, int[1] dim, bool keepdim=False, *, ScalarType? dtype=None) -> Tensor. The representative signature is not exclusive: the original Gems pytest owns the full contract for overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation, and must never be narrowed to this single signature. ALL supplied registered schema strings, verbatim: (1) aten::_sparse_csr_sum.dim_dtype_out(Tensor self, int[1] dim, bool keepdim=False, *, ScalarType? dtype=None, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!); (2) aten::_sparse_csr_sum.dim_dtype(Tensor self, int[1] dim, bool keepdim=False, *, ScalarType? dtype=None) -> Tensor. Semantics derived from the tests: the operator reduces the axes named by dim on a 2-D sparse CSR operand; dim=[0] keeps the columns ((1, cols) result), dim=[1] keeps the rows ((rows, 1) result), and the two-element forms in either order ([0,1], [1,0]) together with the empty list ([]) perform the full reduction; negative axes (-1, -2 and their two-element orders) are accepted. Stored zeros, empty rows, empty columns, int32/int64 index dtypes and zero-stored operands are covered by the structural cases, and those cases assert that the result keeps the operand's index dtype. keepdim keeps its schema default of False, but the native operator rejects keepdim=False, so callers must pass True; the tests call keepdim=True everywhere and assert that omitting it raises. dtype is keyword-only and overrides the accumulation result dtype, exercised by passing dtype (float32, int64 or float64 where supported) over a float32 operand; separately, the out-buffer cases note that with no dtype given the buffer dtype follows the result, not the operand, because integer operands promote their accumulation and an int8 operand yields a long result. An out buffer must match the result's shape, stored count and dtype but not its index values. Errors owned by the pytest: unsupported input dtypes (bool, FP8 e4m3fn/e5m2, which the source reports as lacking a kernel for this operator on the NVIDIA CUDA backend, with the FP8 entries additionally gated on the static FP8 capability flag and both conditions nested under the vendor check, so a backend that does not report the NVIDIA vendor collects an empty list), non-CSR inputs (dense 2-D, COO, dense 1-D), dim elements that are out of range, duplicated, or non-integers (str, float), and the keepdim=False default. The dim_dtype_out overload is the conditional-effect case: out is a required keyword-only tensor that is mutated and aliased by the return (res_out is out), and the kernel rewrites the buffer's crow/col support in place; this definition models only the dim_dtype overload, so the mutating out= form and all conditional effects remain in the original Gems pytest.
